award.caption: Kathak was her first training ground, in a home full of music and learning. Here she is already in costume.
Another early portrait: young, serious and ready.
With Dr. Radhakrishnan, then Vice President of India.
1972. Odissi, learned from Guru Kelucharan Mohapatra, is by now her own language.
An early performance, the musicians seated behind her. She has always worked closely with musicians.
1979, palms joined high above her head.
1981, in profile, her hands close to her face.
In duet with Pandit Durga Lal, a Kathak master, the form she began with.
Bowing low in green and purple.
Both hands at her ears, in white and red.
In red, in profile, fingers already shaped for the next gesture.

kuchipudi.caption: Hands open, eyes steady. The story has already begun.
Green silk, violet light, a pause between two steps.
One hand lifted, the rest of the stage left dark so there is only her to watch.
Her fingers point into the light and the whole frame follows them.
Mid-leap, the blue skirt still catching up with her.
A slow lean in orange, held a moment longer than you expect.
Arms wide over a blue-lit floor.
Down on one knee beside the lamp and the garlanded deity. Kuchipudi grew out of devotion.
The red skirt opens like a fan around her.
Red light, red silk, arms flung wide.

mantra-bhasha.caption: Hands drawn in, weight settled: the quiet before the next movement.
Copper and red, one foot lifted, every line deliberate.
Dark-lined eyes, fingers shaped into a mudra, and she is looking straight at you.
Green beside blue, two dancers moving to the same beat.

santoor-rabab.caption: Santoor on his lap, a half smile, in no hurry to begin.
Pandit Mukesh Sharma at home with the rabab, somewhere in the middle of a thought.

vocal.caption: Brothers in white and printed stoles, one seated with a painted string instrument, the other standing close behind.
